article_text:
10月8日より、BOOK AND SONSで小平雅尋による写真集『Videre Videor』刊行を記念した写真展が開催される。

小平は直感的な撮影行為を続けながら、いかにして対象を認識しシャッターを切るに到るのかについて、省察を続けてきた。本シリーズのタイトル「Videre Videor」は、ルネ・デカルトのコギト命題「われ思う、ゆえにわれあり」へと至る一文、「私は確かに見えると思われ（videre videor）、聞くと思われ（audire videor）、熱を感じると思われる（calescare videor）」を端緒としており、写真に取り組み始めてから約30年、撮り続けてきた本シリーズにおいて、小平はこれらの問いを再考。直感的な撮影を通して個人と世界の根源的な関係性を探る、一種の帰着点を提している。

本展では、1Fと2Fのスペースを使用して24点の作品が展示される。会期に合わせて写真集の先行販売されるほか、初日にはレセプション、10月10日には関連イベントとしてトークイベントも開催されるので会期中に訪れてみてはいかが。

「もし『無意識が見た風景』を写真にするならば、写真家は何をすべきだろうか。 小平雅尋の写真制作は、この問いに対する一つの答えである」 -若山満大（東京ステーションギャラリー学芸員）による寄稿文より

小平雅尋『Videre Videor』 仕様：A4版変型／上製本／96P 執筆：若山満大、近藤耕人 デザイン：田中せり 言語：日本語／英語 定価：5,500円+税 発行：torch press ISBN：978-4-907562-70-0

タイトル

小平雅尋「Videre Videor」

場所

BOOK AND SONS（東京都目黒区鷹番2-13-3 キャトル鷹番）

会期

2026年10月8日（木）〜20日（火） ＊オープニングレセプション 10月8日（木）17:00〜19:00

時間

12:00〜19:00

イベント

トークイベント 10月10日（土）15:00〜16:30（14:30開場） 小平雅尋×若山満大 料金：1,650（税込） 定員：20名 ご予約はこちら

定休日

水曜日

URL

https://bookandsons.com/exhibition/1163/

article_text:
植物に囲まれた屋外庭園で鑑賞体験

音楽家・渋谷慶一郎の最新アルバム『ATAK030 Threshold』の発売 に先駆け、2026年11月3日(火・祝)に一夜限りの先行リスニングイベントが東京都港区高輪のニュウマン高輪 LUFTBAUM「翠の庭」で開催されます。

地上約150mに位置する「翠の庭」には、合計47台のスピーカーを配置した、360°の立体音響を体感できるイマーシブ・オーディオシステムが常設されています。当日はこの音響環境を活かした先行試聴に加え、渋谷慶一郎と音楽批評家の伏見瞬によるトークを実施します。植物に囲まれた地上28階の屋外庭園で、作品の音響世界と制作背景に 触れる時間をお届けします。

イベント詳細 ▶︎ https://1103albumlisteningevent.peatix.com

翌4日から独占先行配信も

また、本イベントは会場となるニュウマン高輪「LUFTBAUM」そして、フランス発の高音質音楽プラットフォーム「Qobuz（コバズ）」との共同開催となり、翌日11月4日（水）からQobuzにて、本アルバムは世界26か国で独占先行配信されます。

「その場でしか生まれない体験を共有できれば」 渋谷さん

渋谷慶一郎はイベントに向けて次のように語っています。 「リリースに先駆けて、東京・高輪のLUFTBAUMでリスニングイベントを開催できることを、とても嬉しく思っています。コンサートホールでも自宅でもない、空に開かれた庭園でこの作品を聴くことで、僕自身もまだ気づいていない作品の表情が現れるのではないかと楽しみにしています。じっと座って目を瞑って耳を傾けるのも良いと思うし、ちょうど日没で明るさが移り変わるのを感じながら生い茂る植物の中を歩きながら聴くのも得難い体験だと思います。植物や風、都市の風景と、360°に広がる音がどのように響き合うのか。皆さんと一緒に、その場でしか生まれない音楽の体験を共有できればと思います。この夜をひとつの始まりとして LUFTBAUMから音楽と都市、空間の新しい関係を探っていきたいと思っています。楽しみにしててください。」

◆開催概要 イベント名：渋谷慶一郎『ATAK030 Threshold』先行リスニング・イベント 日時：2026年11月3日（火・祝）開場 16:30・開始 17:00（19:00終了予定） 会場：ニュウマン高輪 LUFTBAUM 28F 翠の庭 ゲスト：渋谷慶一郎、モデレーター：伏見瞬 料金：3,300円（税込） URL： https://1103albumlisteningevent.peatix.com （美術展ナビ編集班）

article_text:
11月3日に待望のグランドオープンを迎えた皇居三の丸尚蔵館。 開幕展となる特別展「皇室の至宝―美いづるところ」の一部のグッズを、美術展ナビオンラインストアで販売しています。

特別展「皇室の至宝―美いづるところ」公式図録 3,000円

皇居三の丸尚蔵館 (皇居東御苑内) のグランドオープンを記念した特別展「皇室の至宝―美いづるところ」の公式図録です。 出品作品全187件をフルカラーで紹介。同館の研究員らによる論考や作品解説、コラムも掲載された充実の一冊です。

スライドミント缶セット 1,944 円

グランドオープン記念特別展の1期から3期の作品をコレクションできる、スライド缶入りミントのセットです。食べ終わったら、小物入れにしてもいいですね。

総柄ポーチセット 2,420 円

こちらもグランドオープン記念特別展の1期から3期の作品をコレクションできるポーチのセットです。用途に合わせて使い分けながら、名品の魅力を身近に感じられます。

ダイカットクッション 横山華渓《三蟲之図》 6,600 円

修理後初公開となる横山華渓《三蟲之図》がもちもちな手ざわりのクッションになりました。

マスキングロールステッカー 各1,100 円

1枚ずつめくって使えて、順番に出てくる絵柄を楽しめる新感覚の「マスキングロールステッカー」にも《三蟲之図》の絵柄が登場！《天子摂関大臣影 (大臣巻) 》のバージョンもあります。

刺しゅうマスコット 葛飾北斎《西瓜図》／竹内栖鳳《虎》 各1,980 円

葛飾北斎《西瓜図》と竹内栖鳳《虎》を刺しゅうしたボールチェーン付マスコットです。かわいらしい色味が印象的です。

ブランケット 《龍蛟躍四溟》 3,850 円

迫力のある《龍蛟躍四溟》がデザインされたふかふかのブランケットは、肌寒い季節のお供にはもちろん、インテリアを彩るグッズとしても活躍してくれそうです。

そして、特別展「皇室の至宝―美いづるところ」の オープニングを飾る前期展示では、今年の正倉院の開封に合わせ、11件の正倉院宝物が出品されています。それを記念して販売された 数量限定のオリジナル注染手ぬぐいセット を美術展ナビオンラインストアの 正倉院展特設売店「天平」 で取り扱い中です。

また、11月9日（月）まで奈良国立博物館で開催される「第78回正倉院展」のグッズも販売中です。 正倉院展特設売店「天平」 もあわせてのぞいてみてはいかがでしょうか。

皇居三の丸尚蔵館のグッズはこちら▶

"与专业或非专业演员合作，是我拍电影时最享受的事情之一，但也是最困难的事情之一。就《新来的人》而言，我们选择完全由当地人来出演。这意味着一个漫长的寻找演员的过程，主要在塔帕胡拉帕（Tapijulapa）和奥索洛坦（Oxolotán），即塔科塔尔帕（Tacotalpa）市镇的塔巴斯科（Tabasco）地区进行。我们在那里与小演员们开展了表演工作坊，起初与演员同伴加夫列拉·卡托尔（Gabriela Cartol）合作，随后与米里亚姆·巴尔德拉斯（Miriam Balderas）合作了更长时间。在这些工作坊中，我们专注于表演训练。我们必须从零开始教他们。随后成年人也加入进来，从而营造出一个充满即兴创作和学习的空间。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在那里，我们共同探索了一种工作方式，向演员传递工具，让他们懂得如何在场景和游戏中保持专注，而不必担心摄像机。那是最大的挑战，但我感觉这种选择——与当地演员合作——为电影赋予了独特性。普适性存在于故事本身之中，但将事件置于一个特定的世界里，赋予了电影个性、色彩、风味和独特的宇宙。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": {"type": "paragraph", "text": "CP：最近我们听到亚历杭德罗·冈萨雷斯·伊纳里图和吉尔莫·德尔·托罗等导演公开代表他们这一代人进行反省，痛心于他们留给年轻一代的世界陷入了严峻的境地（在环境、社会政治等方面）。罗德里戈，我想请教你是否也有过类似的心情，如果是的话，这对比最终呈现出来的电影产生了怎样的影响？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部电影改编自劳拉·桑图略几年前写的一本书，小说名叫《他们随风而来》（Llegaron con el viento）。激发这一创作、如今又支撑起整部电影的情感，与我们自身的童年经历直接相关。我和劳拉都曾是流亡儿童，我们很小的时候就来到了墨西哥，当时我们的家庭由于政治原因被迫移民，当时乌拉圭的一场政变将军方推上了权力宝座。可以说，移民的主题、渴望讲述人们被迫流离失所的困境及其对儿童世界影响的愿望，是我们创作这部电影的主要情感动力。", "translated": true}, {"type": "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "CP：请向我解释一下影片在墨西哥评级时遇到的问题。目前，据我所知它被评为12岁以上限制级，且RTC（国家广播电视电影局）并未给出明确的理由。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本质上，我们对所获得的评级持异议，因为我们认为这部电影无论在内容还是形式上都明显面向儿童。RTC的评估在我们看来是一个判断失误。事实正是如此，《Los nuevos》曾入选全球多个专注于儿童领域的电影节，有时面向6岁以上，有时面向8岁以上。我们不明白为什么对于墨西哥儿童来说就会有所不同。我们与他们有过一些信息交流，但我们觉得回应一直很模糊，没有指出任何决定该决定的具体场景或元素，也没有提供上诉的可能。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管分级只是一项建议，但我们认为它对电影的发行推广产生了非常负面的影响。考虑到专为年轻观众打造的墨西哥电影几乎为零，这一决定着实令人遗憾。我们非常希望这部电影除了登陆院线外，还能在文化中心和教学机构等非主流巡回放映渠道中传播，因为我们觉得电影展现了友谊、团结和同理心等对儿童非常重要的价值观。给我们的分级起到了阻碍作用，而非激发儿童走进影厅。不过，我们仍期盼这一决定能够得到重新评估。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.cinepremiere.com.mx/uploads/2026/10/los-nuevos-ficm-2026-5-900x506.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Cine PREMIERE", "translated": {"type": "paragraph", "text": "CP：墨西哥电影资料馆（IMCINE）最新统计年鉴提供了一个有些负面的数据：2025年只制作了2部专为儿童观众构思的墨西哥故事片，其中一部恰好就是你的作品。你如何看待这种专为儿童打造的墨西哥电影的匮乏？难道是我们的行业认为这类电影是“低人一等的”电影，还是说这些故事根本就无法吸引当今活跃的墨西哥电影人？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这个问题我无法回答你。这只会是对其他人选择拍或不拍儿童电影动机的种种猜测。但我可以跟你谈谈我自己的创作过程。对对我而言，转变拍摄语调是一个挑战。这意味着必须进行许多深度的自我审视，去寻找一种能让儿童理解并产生共情的方式来呈现那些实质性的、重要的话题，同时又不能忽视这是一部必须充满娱乐性和激动人心的儿童电影。这绝非易事，跟绝大多数由儿童组成的演员阵容合作也同样不容易。这是一项不同的工作，需要另一种耐心，在对待他们时需要另一种细腻，并在创作过程中寻找游戏的乐趣。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "现在电影已经制作完成，我们也看到了非常美妙的观众反响——人们在笑，孩子们在享受它——我觉得自己跳出舒适区、勇敢尝试其他叙事方式是值得的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Los nuevos》作为FICM 2026官方展映单元的一部分迎来了它的墨西哥首映。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.cinepremiere.com.mx/wp-content/uploads/2017/08/CP-favicon-512.jpg'", "alt": "作者", "caption": "", "credit": "Cine El director Rodrigo Plá y la guionista Laura Santullo, quienes asistieron al FICM 2026 para presentar Los nuevos —el más reciente largometraje de su extensa colaboración— informaron en conferencia de prensa que dicha película había recibido una clasificación para mayores de 12 años de parte de la Dirección General de Radio, Televisión y Cinematografía (RTC). Sin embargo, añadieron, hasta ese momento no les habían dado una explicación concreta de por qué aquélla, una película pensada para las infancias, presuntamente no era apta para niños."}, {"type": "quote", "text": "« Los nuevos ha sido seleccionada en diversos festivales del mundo especializados en la infancia, a veces para mayores de seis años, a veces para mayores de ocho. Artículos

FICM 2026: Los nuevos, una película para las infancias, ¿no apta para niños?

Antonio G. Spíndola

Rodrigó Plá, director de 'Los nuevos', platicó con Cine PREMIERE sobre aquellas vivencias personales que lo conectan con el tema de la migración y sobre la lucha por descartar una injustificada clasificación.

En el marco de la 24 edición del Festival Internacional de Cine de Morelia, el estreno de uno de los títulos mexicanos en competencia vino acompañado de una noticia nada grata para sus responsables. El director Rodrigo Plá y la guionista Laura Santullo, quienes asistieron al FICM 2026 para presentar Los nuevos —el más reciente largometraje de su extensa colaboración— informaron en conferencia de prensa que dicha película había recibido una clasificación para mayores de 12 años de parte de la Dirección General de Radio, Televisión y Cinematografía (RTC). Sin embargo, añadieron, hasta ese momento no les habían dado una explicación concreta de por qué aquélla, una película pensada para las infancias, presuntamente no era apta para niños.

« Los nuevos ha sido seleccionada en diversos festivales del mundo especializados en la infancia, a veces para mayores de seis años, a veces para mayores de ocho. No entendemos por qué sería distinto para los niños mexicanos», explicó Plá en entrevista exclusiva con Cine PREMIERE. «Hemos tenido un intercambio de mensajes con ellos [la RTC] y sentimos que la respuesta ha sido opaca, sin un señalamiento de escenas o elementos concretos que hayan determinado la decisión, y sin la posibilidad de apelar».

FICM

Lee también: FICM 2026 – Guillermo del Toro siente necesario el reestreno del El laberinto del Fauno

Basada en la novela Llegaron con el viento , escrita por la propia Laura Santullo, esta película nos cuenta la historia de Tiana, Mateo y Tomás, tres niños de una comunidad rural a la que llegan numerosas familias desplazadas por culpa de la misma compañía minera que ahora vuelve a acechar, amenazando con seguir esparciendo su mancha contaminante. Será entonces labor de aquellos infantes salvar el día, a través de un largo viaje por el campo donde afortunadamente contarán con la protección de una amigable can llamada Nube.

Los nuevos (selección oficial del FICM 2026, en la Sección de Largometraje Mexicano) tuvo su premiere mundial en agosto de 2026, como parte de la programación del Festival Internacional de Cine de Locarno, específicamente dentro de una sección enfocada en el público infantil. En cuanto a galardones, ahí mismo obtuvo una mención especial en la categoría «Pardo for Change», que premia aquellos títulos que fomentan la concientización en torno a temas ambientales.

«Te diría que es el tema de la migración, el deseo de hablar sobre la problemática del desplazamiento forzoso de las personas y su consecuencia sobre el mundo infantil, el principal sentimiento que nos motivó para hacer la película», nos compartió Plá. «[Por otro lado] también hay en la historia una clara preocupación por el cuidado del medio ambiente y sobre todo una exposición de la codicia de unos pocos que se adueñan de los bienes que son de todos».

Lean a continuación nuestra entrevista completa con Rodrigo Plá, a propósito de la participación de Los nuevos en el FICM 2026. El también director de El otro Tom y Un monstruo de mil cabezas nos contó sobre su experiencia trabajando con niños actores y dirigiendo por primera vez en su carrera una película cuyo público más importante es el de temprana edad. Asimismo nos platicó sobre aquellas vivencias personales que lo conectan con el tema de la migración y sobre la lucha por disuadir a la RTC de su injustificada clasificación.

Lee también: El otro Tom, un cuestionamiento al abuso en la medicación psiquiátrica

CP: ¿Cuáles fueron los mayores retos y cuál fue tu estrategia no sólo para trabajar con niños en el rodaje, sino también para poner todos tus recursos fílmicos al servicio de un punto de vista tan luminoso e inocente, pero a la vez tan arrojado y envalentonado, como lo es justamente el de un niño?

El trabajo con actores profesionales, o no profesionales , es de las cosas que más disfruto de hacer películas, pero de las más difíciles también. En el caso de Los nuevos , nos decantamos por realizarla en su totalidad con gente del lugar. Eso signiﬁcó un proceso largo de búsqueda de los intérpretes, principalmente en Tapijulapa y Oxolotán, en el municipio de Tacotalpa, Tabasco. Allí hicimos talleres de actuación con los pequeños, en colaboración con compañeras actrices, como Gabriela Cartol en un inicio, y después durante más tiempo con Miriam Balderas. En estos talleres nos concentramos en el entrenamiento actoral. Había que enseñarles desde cero. Luego se sumaron los adultos, y se generó un espacio de improvisación y de aprendizaje.

Allí, fuimos buscando en conjunto una forma de trabajo, transmitiendo herramientas a los actores para que supieran estar presentes en la escena, en el juego, sin preocuparse de la cámara. Ese fue el mayor reto, pero siento que esta elección, trabajar con actores locales, le aporta a la película singularidad. Lo universal está presente en la historia en sí, pero ubicar los sucesos en un mundo especíﬁco le da carácter a la película, le aporta un color, un sabor, un universo único.

Lee también: FICM 2026 – La bola negra – Crítica de la película

CP: Últimamente hemos escuchado a directores como Alejandro González Iñárritu y Guillermo del Toro que públicamente maniﬁestan un mea culpa en nombre de toda su generación, por el grave estado del mundo (a nivel ambiental, sociopolítico, etc.) que ellos le están dejando a las generaciones más jóvenes. Quisiera, Rodrigo, que me contaras si has tenido un sentimiento similar y, en caso aﬁrmativo, de qué manera eso inﬂuyó para lo que esta película terminó siendo.

La película es una adaptación de un libro que escribió Laura Santullo hace algunos años, la novela se llama Llegaron con el viento . Y el sentimiento que animó esa escritura y que ahora sostiene también la película se vincula directamente con nuestra propia infancia. Ambos, Laura y yo, fuimos niños exiliados, llegamos a México muy pequeños, cuando nuestras familias se vieron obligadas a emigrar por causas políticas, cuando un golpe de estado llevó a los militares al poder en Uruguay. Te diría que es el tema de la migración, el deseo de hablar sobre la problemática del desplazamiento forzoso de las personas y su consecuencia sobre el mundo infantil, el principal sentimiento que nos motivó para hacer la película.

Claro que, como bien señalas, también hay en la historia una clara preocupación por el cuidado del medio ambiente y sobre todo una exposición de la codicia de unos pocos que se adueñan de los bienes que son de todos. Creemos que ambos temas, la migración y el medio ambiente, son conversaciones que hay que abrir al mundo infantil.

Lee también: FICM 2026 – Los Cuarón se reúnen para presentar Campeón Gabacho

CP: Explícame, por favor, el problema que hubo con la clasiﬁcación de la película en México. Por lo pronto, tengo entendido que recibió una clasiﬁcación para mayores de 12 años y que la RTC no ha brindado una justificación clara al respecto.

En esencia, discrepamos con la clasificación que se nos ha dado, porque consideramos que la película está claramente destinada a los niños y las niñas en su contenido y en su forma. La apreciación de la RTC nos parece un error de juicio. Tan es así que Los nuevos ha sido seleccionada en diversos festivales del mundo especializados en la infancia, a veces para mayores de seis años, a veces para mayores de ocho. No entendemos por qué sería distinto para los niños mexicanos. Hemos tenido un intercambio de mensajes con ellos y sentimos que la respuesta ha sido opaca, sin un señalamiento de escenas o elementos concretos que hayan determinado la decisión, y sin la posibilidad de apelar.

Si bien la clasificación es una recomendación, creemos que afecta de manera muy negativa las posibilidades de circulación de la película. Tomando en cuenta la casi nula existencia de películas mexicanas destinadas al público más joven, es una verdadera lástima esta decisión. Nos encantaría que además de llegar a los cines la película se moviera también en un circuito alternativo, en centros culturales y de enseñanza, porque sentimos que la película expone valores como la amistad, la solidaridad y la empatía, que son relevantes para la infancia. La clasificación que nos han dado disuade, en lugar de estimular, la presencia infantil en las salas. Sin embargo, aún tenemos la esperanza de que haya una revisión de la decisión tomada.

FICM

Entrevista en video: FICM 2026 – Seis meses en el edificio rosa con azul, de Bruno Santamaría

CP: Un dato un tanto negativo que ofrece el último Anuario Estadístico del IMCINE es que en 2025 sólo se produjeron DOS largometrajes mexicanos pensados para el público infantil y uno de ellos era justamente el tuyo. ¿Qué opinas de esta carencia de cine mexicano destinado a niñas y niños? ¿Será acaso que nuestra industria lo considera un cine “menor” o simplemente no son historias que en general atraigan a las y los cineastas mexicanos hoy en días activos?

Es una pregunta que no puedo contestarte. Sólo serían conjeturas sobre los motivos de otras personas para hacer o no hacer un cine destinado a la infancia. Pero puedo hablarte de mi propio proceso. Para mí el cambio de registro ha sido un reto. Implicó preguntarse muchas cosas de manera profunda, buscar una narrativa que pusiera al alcance de la comprensión y de la empatía de los niños temas que son sustantivos, que son importantes, pero sin perder de vista que se estaba haciendo una película para niños que debía ser entretenida y emocionante. No fue tarea fácil, como tampoco lo fue trabajar con un elenco mayoritariamente infantil. Es un trabajo distinto, que requiere otra paciencia, otra delicadeza en el trato y una búsqueda de lo lúdico en el proceso.

Ahora que la película ya está lista, y que hemos visto un lindo resultado con el público, que la gente ríe, que los niños y las niñas la disfrutan, creo que valió la pena el moverme de lugar, el animarme a probar otras formas de contar.

Los nuevos tuvo su premiere mexicana como parte de la selección oficial del FICM 2026.

Antonio G. Spíndola Tengo muy mala memoria. Por solidaridad con mis recuerdos, opto por perderme también. De preferencia, en una sala de cine.

article_text:
Egypt’s El Gouna Film Festival heads into its ninth edition with a mix of major international titles, including Cannes prize winners “All of a Sudden” and “Ben’imana,” major star power, and the Red Sea glitz woven into its DNA.

Co-founder and executive director Amr Mansi wants to expand upon those founding elements, broadening GFF’s industry ambitions and establishing new partnerships in its push to become a major player in the regional film space beyond the annual nine-day event.

Related Stories

Isabelle Huppert Vampire Film ‘The Blood Countess’ Was Cut Against Director’s Wishes, Ulrike Ottinger Tells Tokyo Event

Tarantino Fired Mélanie Laurent From 'Inglourious Basterds' After 'Terrible' Table Read and Axed Isabelle Huppert for Not Showing Up: 'I Don't Owe You Jack S---'

“We want the industry to be our hero,” Mansi stresses in an interview with Variety . “We’re trying to build the ecosystem with filmmakers, creators and everyone in the industry, but at the same time balancing it with the glam, etc. At the end of the day, commercial partners are needed to keep the festival alive to showcase filmmakers.”

That expansion continues to evolve, with CineGouna , the festival’s industry arm, growing across financing, talent development and its market, while moving into television and streaming series for the first time this year.

CineGouna Funding received more than 310 submissions from across the Arab world, selecting 13 projects in development and six films in post-production. A new Egyptian Voices initiative adds four homegrown projects receiving support in pitching, packaging and co-production. Proposed by Egyptian screenwriter and CineGouna Forum head Mariam Naoum, CineGouna Series drew more than 125 submissions for six spots in its new development lab and industry market.

Running alongside GFF’s expanding industry ambitions is its longstanding “Cinema for Humanity” mission, reflected, for example, in the newly launched Safe Harbour MENA initiative, which brings four displaced filmmakers from the region to El Gouna for training and networking. “We are trying to be the voice for the people who don’t have a voice, a place to share, to tell their stories,” Mansi emphasizes.

CineGouna dates back to GFF’s inaugural edition in 2017 and has grown to include funding, a forum, a market and an emerging talent program, with new initiatives planned for its landmark tenth edition next year.

For Mansi, the push to establish GFF as an industry hub and expand its regional and international reach ultimately serves the more tangible goal of funding more filmmakers and their projects.

“I believe with our positioning, we can increase the amount of money that we get every year to be able to support more filmmakers and more perspectives,” he asserts.

Commercial partners are increasingly part of that equation. Mansi points to sponsors providing direct grants and channeling more of the festival’s commercial backing straight to filmmakers. “This was never a conversation that I could have dreamed of five, six years ago,” he reflects.

GFF is also building long-term partnerships with festivals abroad. In August, it announced a strategic partnership with the Zurich Film Festival focused on collaboration across programming, as well as exchanging and recommending films, talent, and jury members. Mansi hopes to establish similar collaborations elsewhere, helping emerging talent move more easily between festivals, make industry connections, and create opportunities for career growth internationally.

With more festivals competing for films, projects and talent across the SWANA region (Southwest Asia and North Africa), Mansi says the proximity of El Gouna’s venues offers the advantage of screenings, meetings and networking happening within minutes of one another, a departure from many international festivals.

The festival is also drawing a larger audience each year. GFF sold more than 40,000 tickets and issued more than 7,000 accreditations last year, Mansi says, with attendance up 30% from the previous edition. Its 1,400-seat outdoor plaza was full each day of the festival, a level of turnout he notes GFF had never previously seen.

Mansi also wants the El Gouna Film Festival to reach audiences who may never make it to its Red Sea locale. An agreement with Cairo arthouse cinema Zawya brings part of its program to the capital as the festival runs miles and miles away. Official broadcast partner Al Nahar Television Network, meanwhile, is set to provide daily coverage of festival activities across Egypt. GFF will also stream selected panels and masterclasses on its digital platforms, part of a broader push to make the festival and its industry conversations more accessible beyond El Gouna to the wider Egyptian public and beyond.

Those efforts feed into a longer-term plan to expand El Gouna’s regional and global footprint beyond its annual festival. With its tenth edition on the horizon, Mansi wants to build a year-round film and industry meeting place that can support filmmakers, connect industry players, and extend GFF’s reach long after each edition ends.

article_text:
Ian McKellen has shared a tribute to his “ X-Men ” series co-star and longtime friend Patrick Stewart , who died Wednesday at the age of 86.

McKellen and Stewart’s relationship goes back decades to their time as young theater actors with the Royal Shakespeare Company. They became inseparably tied together for general audiences when they starred opposite one another in Marvel’s “X-Men” film series, playing the frenemies Magneto and Professor X. Over the years, the two have shared a public friendship, often appearing at premieres for each other’s work and serving as two of British theater’s leading global ambassadors. In 2009, they starred in a West End production of “Waiting for Godot.”

“Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end. You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues,” McKellen wrote in a statement posted to social media. “He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love.”

McKellen went on to recall Stewart’s decision to play Jean-Luc Picard on “Star Trek: The Next Generation” in the late ’80s — a role that solidified his presence in Hollywood and made him a household name for general audiences.

“We first met as ambitious young actors with the Royal Shakespeare Company half a century ago but we weren’t in the same productions. My first strong memory was a few years later, meeting him in the street in central London when he told me about an offer to take over a leading part in ‘Star Trek’. ‘But Patrick think of your stage career in the UK. Do you really want to risk—getting lost in Hollywood for years and years?'” McKellen continued. “Well, he took the risk and thank goodness for us all that he did for not just his devoted Trekkies but film and theatre audiences, who marvelled at his using international celebrity to star in a string of cinema successes (‘X-Men’ of course) and in great classical plays by Shakespeare, Ibsen, Arthur Miller, Peter Shaffer, Pinter and Beckett at Stratford-upon-Avon, in London’s West End and on Broadway.”

“America was his adopted home, where he met his adored Sunny who has cared for him through sickness and health, through thick and thin. But he never forsook his origins: and the proudest achievement of the most respected and beloved actor of his generation on either side of the Atlantic, was his appointment as Chancellor of Huddersfield University in Yorkshire.”

McKellen and Stewart will appear together onscreen for a final time in Marvel’s “Avengers: Doomsday,” releasing to theaters in December. The two reprise their respective roles of Magneto and Professor X.

article_text:
Amanda Jiang , Joey Phillips (“Outlander”), Richard Brake (“Game of Thrones,” “The Mandalorian,” “Kingsman: The Secret Service,” “Barbarian”) and Shayne Ward (“The Good Ship Murder,” “Coronation Street”) will lead the cast of gothic romance and supernatural thriller “Dracula: The Crimson Code,” which has started filming.

The contemporary female-led Dracula reimagining is directed by Andrea M. Catinella and written by Enrico Tessarin. The film is set in contemporary London and the English countryside.

Related Stories

Spotify Inks Licensing Deal With Believe Music for AI Remixing Tool

Spotify Has Removed 50 Million AI Slop Tracks From Recommendations This Year

Jiang stars as Countess Isolde Dragomir, a centuries-old vampire aristocrat at the center of London’s most exclusive social circles. Her glamorous Crimson Code soirées conceal an ancient conflict between two vampire bloodlines — the Dragomirs and the Howes — and a centuries-old desire for revenge against the man who murdered the great love of her life.

When Isolde kills the son of her old enemy, she draws him back into her world. But her plans are disrupted by the arrival of Theo Mercer, a man she recognizes as the reincarnation of the lover she lost centuries earlier.

Theo, however, is not simply Adrian returned. He is his own man — forcing Isolde to confront whether she can finally let go of the past.

The film is produced by Tessarin, Jiang, Catinella and Carla Fuschillo for Starmist Films , whose first feature “City of Masks” has its world premiere in London on Oct. 29.

Jiang said in a statement, “I have always been drawn to gothic atmosphere, the theatricality of it and the way those worlds can create a sense of mystery, danger and desire. That was very much part of what inspired ‘City of Masks,’ and it is something I wanted to explore even further with ‘The Crimson Code.’

“With ‘Dracula,’ we have the opportunity to take that love of gothic storytelling into a much larger world. Isolde is powerful, dangerous and deeply vulnerable, and at the heart of the film is a story about love, revenge and the possibility of choosing a different future.”

article_text:
Films and events

Laugh

Wicker

Olivia Colman gives yet another bravura performance in this delightfully offbeat comedy, playing an outcast from her village who orders herself a wicker husband.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Directors-screenwriters Alex Huston Fischer, Eleanor Wilson

With Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård, Elizabeth Debicki

USA 2026. 105min

Courtesy of Black Bear

Language English

Access information

Thursday 8 October 17:45

Audio description

Closed Captions (CC) via WatchWord smart glasses

Saturday 10 October 12:00

Audio description

Wednesday 14 October 15:00

Audio description

Descriptive subtitles

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

Fisherwoman is unmarried, allegedly smelly, constantly teased by her small-minded neighbours and desperate to keep to herself. But when she decides to see what life would be like with a very particular kind of mail-order husband, what arrives (a statuesque Alexander Skarsgård) soon sparks jealousy and creates chaos. Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson’s wonderfully eccentric fable is, at its core, a gentle love story.

Isabel Moir

Content advice

Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury, nudity, and sex.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

The Idiot(s)

Aimee Lou Wood and Johnny Flynn are superb as Anna and Fyodor Dostoevsky in Małgorzata Szumowska and Michał Englert’s acerbic and joyful period film.

Wild Horse Nine

Martin McDonagh continues to mine the absurdities and complexities of male relationships in a film that brims with energy and is sure to delight.

The Debut

For LFF 2026’s curtain call, writer-director Jesse Eisenberg delivers a rapturous and raucously funny love letter to community theatre, featuring a luminous lead performance by Julianne Moore.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 在艺术家的MCA展览期间，印有原住民人物和图案的茶巾、烟灰缸、餐具和衣物每天都被亲手送来或邮寄而来，此前他发出了征集呼吁。警告：本文包含种族主义和冒犯性器物及图像的描绘……

article_text:
F ive months ago Indigenous artist Tony Albert made a public request for donations of Aboriginalia – souvenirs, homewares and other objects depicting Aboriginal people and designs, often as caricatures, that were created and sold by non-Indigenous people.

It was a request that accompanied his career-spanning Not a Souvenir exhibition at the Museum of Contemporary Art (MCA) in Sydney, which featured 4,400 objects from the artist’s own collection – one he started in the 1980s as a child.

Now, in the exhibition’s closing days, the MCA is packaging and shipping 2,000 more items donated by the public to Albert’s studio in Brisbane.

“I have been genuinely overwhelmed by the generosity and response,” says Albert via email from Paris, where he is on a month-long artist residency. The 45-year-old, who has family connections to the Girramay, Kuku Yalanji and Yidindji peoples, has been personally in touch with the people who brought stuff in.

“What has moved me most is not simply the number of objects donated, but the personal stories and conversations that have accompanied them,” he says. “There is something incredibly powerful and healing about people wanting to confront this history and entrusting me with these objects, so that together we can give them new meaning.”

Carolyn Ienna, a 63-year-old Wiradjuri artist and activist from Sydney, dropped off a painted image of an Aboriginal man with a spear last week. They found it in a council pickup collection over a decade ago.

“I’d look at it and feel sad, but I didn’t have a name for it,” says Ienna. “I didn’t know what Aboriginalia was.” When they discovered it, it felt like the previous owners were “throwing away an Aboriginal person”.

“I don’t think [people] understand the complexities of not only the trauma of colonisation, and how different Aboriginal people may see this Aboriginalia, but also the propaganda of it,” says Ienna.

One of the aims of Albert’s Aboriginalia call-out is to take items like this out of circulation; another is to reappropriate them through his practice.

Lesley Pepper, who travelled from Dunedin in New Zealand to see the exhibition, dropped off a set of serviettes, placemats and four porcelain plates that she has had for “30 or 40 years”.

“They were probably purchased here in New Zealand, in op-shops,” says the 67-year-old. “I have a Māori background, and when I first bought them I felt that I was bringing them home, as a sign of respect.”

One of her plates depicts a young Aboriginal woman, which Pepper says reminded her of herself. “[The woman] was probably never asked if her image could be used,” she says, remorsefully.

It wasn’t an easy decision to give away pieces she had cherished for decades, but “when Tony said he wants to get them out of circulation, I thought ‘yep OK’, they have to come down. If that’s what he’s asking, that’s what you do.”

Items have been delivered to the MCA every day of the exhibition, says assistant curator Antares Wells. “Yesterday we received a donation of a nearly one-metre-tall figurine depicting an Aboriginal man with a spear,” she says. “One donation alone had 120 plates, cups and saucers depicting Aboriginalia, another had 200 beer coasters.”

after newsletter promotion

Unpacking items has been a more positive experience than Wells initially imagined. “When we launched the appeal, we didn’t know what the response would be from the Australian public – and in this political and cultural climate the first thing I personally thought was I really hope that we’re not exposing Tony to hate mail,” she says.

“But I haven’t seen one piece of hate mail and I think that has actually been incredibly inspiring and very powerful.”

Kathryn Hopps, who lives in Canberra, made a detour to Sydney on the way back from visiting family to hand in a pair of silky Australiana scarves she had inherited from her grandmother.

“They were classic 1970s and 80s Australian souvenirs with kangaroos and wattle and Uluru, and pictures of Aboriginal people and designs all mixed in together,” says the 46-year-old. “I immediately recognised that this was not something I wanted to wear … I don’t think my grandma had any idea.

“The only reason I held on to them is because I thought they should be in a museum,” she says. “We can learn from these things, which is why I was delighted to find out about Tony Albert’s exhibition and the opportunity to donate … It felt like a significant thing to do.”

Though the MCA’s donation boxes will be removed after the exhibition closes on 19 October, Wells says the gallery will “gratefully accept” any further Aboriginalia, which will then be passed on to Albert.

Collecting has been integral to Albert’s life and artistic practice since he was young, he says. “I don’t think that will ever change, but what continues to evolve is my understanding of these objects and the possibilities they hold for telling stories, challenging perceptions and creating something meaningful from a difficult history.”

A donated object that really stood out for him is a 1930s ceramic shaving mug in the shape of a caricature of an Aboriginal man’s face.

“I find it astonishing that someone would have wanted this object sitting in their bathroom, and used it as part of their everyday routine,” he says. “These objects are actually incredibly rare and quite valuable, but what fascinates me most is what they reveal about the way Aboriginal people have been represented and how casually these images became part of Australian domestic life.”

Tony Albert: Not a Souvenir is on at the Museum of Contemporary Art, Sydney until 19 October 2026

editorial_title_zh: 摄影师松尾修出版拍摄故乡佐世保的新作摄影集《Other Shore》。收录了往返于彼岸与此岸的78幅作品

article_text:
写真家・松尾修の新作写真集『Other Shore』が刊行された。松尾が生まれ育った長崎県佐世保市を舞台に、2023年から2026年にかけて撮影した身近な人々と風景78点をモノクロームで収録する。

米海軍が駐留する基地の街であり、日本の高度経済成長を支えた造船の街でもある佐世保。松尾は商業写真家として東京で活動する一方、長年にわたって故郷へ通い、そこに暮らす人々や風景を撮影してきた。代表的な連作「サセボプロジェクト」をはじめ、その制作では一貫して「写真」と「写真を残そうとする人間の心」を見つめている。

タイトルの「Other Shore＝向こう岸」が示唆するように、本作で松尾は東京と佐世保、過去と現在、虚と実、そして写真の「向こう側」と「こちら側」とを往還する。カメラの前に確かに存在したはずの身近な人物や風景は、写真として定着された瞬間、「いたかもしれない人々」へと姿を変えていく。そこから浮かび上がるのは、記録でありながら現実そのものではないという、写真というメディアが本来的に抱える不可思議さだ。

巻末には、松尾自身によるエッセイ「滅びの予感」を日本語と英語で収録。佐世保という街の歴史と、写真というメディアの本質をめぐる作家の思索が、写真群と呼応する。また、布張りの上製本による表紙には、「向こう側の世界」を象徴するミラープレートを貼り込み、写真集そのものの造本にも作品のコンセプトを反映させた。装丁はThere Thereの渡辺和音が担当している。

松尾は1970年、長崎県佐世保市生まれ、東京在住。これまでに『他人のアルバム』『写真論』のほか、「サセボプロジェクト」として『坂道とクレーン』『誰かのアイドル』『HEAVY METAL』『17』などを刊行している。

松尾修『Other Shore』 価格：6600円（税込） 発行：CLOCK Inc.

In reality, Black ranchers, pioneers, soldiers, and outlaws were instrumental in shaping the frontier; their true stories are long overshadowed by Hollywood’s legendary imagery."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Black filmmakers and performers have long challenged that narrative. From the pioneering work of Woody Strode and the subversive humor of Mel Brooks to the Blaxploitation Westerns of the 1970s and contemporary reinterpretations by Quentin Tarantino and Jeymes Samuel, the genre has gradually expanded to embrace stories once pushed to its margins."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Documentary filmmakers have also played an essential role in reclaiming this history, turning their cameras toward the real cowboys and cowgirls whose communities have kept Western traditions alive for generations."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "As Black Western culture experiences renewed visibility through music, fashion, photography, and cinema, these films offer a revealing look at the people who helped shape the American West, both historically and today."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The following films and documentaries trace the evolution of Black representation in the Western genre, from overlooked Hollywood classics and revisionist revenge tales to contemporary celebrations of Black cowboy culture."}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "SERGEANT RUTLEDGE – 1960 Image Credit: Everett Collection Directed by John Ford, Woody Strode stars as a Black cavalry sergeant falsely accused of rape and murder on the American frontier. article_text:
While cinema has spent over a hundred years defining the American West with iconic dusty towns, epic landscapes, and solitary white cowboys, this silver-screen myth leaves out a crucial chapter. In reality, Black ranchers, pioneers, soldiers, and outlaws were instrumental in shaping the frontier; their true stories are long overshadowed by Hollywood’s legendary imagery.

Black filmmakers and performers have long challenged that narrative. From the pioneering work of Woody Strode and the subversive humor of Mel Brooks to the Blaxploitation Westerns of the 1970s and contemporary reinterpretations by Quentin Tarantino and Jeymes Samuel, the genre has gradually expanded to embrace stories once pushed to its margins.

Documentary filmmakers have also played an essential role in reclaiming this history, turning their cameras toward the real cowboys and cowgirls whose communities have kept Western traditions alive for generations.

As Black Western culture experiences renewed visibility through music, fashion, photography, and cinema, these films offer a revealing look at the people who helped shape the American West, both historically and today.

The following films and documentaries trace the evolution of Black representation in the Western genre, from overlooked Hollywood classics and revisionist revenge tales to contemporary celebrations of Black cowboy culture.

SERGEANT RUTLEDGE – 1960 Image Credit: Everett Collection Directed by John Ford, Woody Strode stars as a Black cavalry sergeant falsely accused of rape and murder on the American frontier. One of the earliest major Hollywood Westerns centered on a Black hero, the film confronts racial prejudice while celebrating the overlooked history of the Buffalo Soldiers.

BLACK RODEO – 1972 Image Credit: Everett Collection Documentary about a rodeo that takes place, for the most part, in Harlem, New York City. Directed by Jeff Kanew featuring Muhammad Ali, Archie Wycoff and Clarence Gonzalez.

BUCK AND THE PREACHER – 1972 Image Credit: Everett Collection A wagon master and a con-man preacher help freed slaves dogged by cheap-labor agents out West. Co-Directed by Joseph Sargent and Sidney Poitier, the film stars Harry Belafonte, Ruby Dee, and Poitier.

BLAZING SADDLES – 1974 Image Credit: Everett Collection In order to ruin a western town and steal their land, a corrupt politician appoints a black sheriff, who promptly becomes his most formidable adversary. Directed by Mel Brooks, starring Cleavon Little, Gene Wilder, and Slim Pickens.

THOMASINE AND BUSHROD – 1974 Image Credit: Everett Collection The exploits of 1910s bounty hunter Thomasine and bandit Bushrod, who after rekindling their old romance, take to robbing banks to survive, stealing from rich whites and sharing their loot with the poor on the harsh frontier. Directed by Gordon Parks Jr., starring Vonetta McGee and Max Julien.

JOSHUA – 1976 Image Credit: Everett Collection A black soldier returns from fighting for the Union in the Civil War only to find out that his mother has been murdered by a gang of white thugs. He becomes a bounty hunter, determined to track down and kill the men who killed his mother. Directed by Larry G. Spangler, starring Fred Williamson.

BUFFALO SOLDIERS – 1997 Image Credit: TNT The all-Black US Cavalry Troop H pursues Apache warrior Victorio while dealing with racial bigotry and myths about their designated enemies. Directed by Charles Haid, starring Danny Glover and Glynn Turman.

DJANGO UNCHAINED – 2012 Image Credit: Andrew Cooper/©Weinstein Company With the help of a German bounty hunter, a freed slave sets out to rescue his wife from a brutal plantation owner in Mississippi. Directed by Quentin Tarantino, starring Jamie Foxx, Leonardo DiCaprio, Kerry Washington, and Samuel L. Jackson.

THE HARDER THEY FALL – 2021 Image Credit: David Lee/Netflix When an outlaw discovers his enemy is being released from prison, he reunites his gang to seek revenge. Directed by Jeymes Samuel, starring Danielle Deadwyler, Jonathan Majors, Zazie Beetz, and RJ Cyler.

HIGH HORSE: THE BLACK COWBOY – 2025 Image Credit: William Gray/PEACOCK The Three-Part Documentary Hailing From Monkeypaw Productions and Universal Television Alternative Studio Celebrates the Powerful Heritage of the Black Cowboy Culture.

article_text:
DOC NYC announced its influential short lists Wednesday, often a reliable gauge of which documentaries are connecting with awards voters as Oscar season heats up.

Among the films making the festival’s short list of features: Ava DuVernay’s 14 th ; You Can See Everything , the Elizabeth Holmes-focused documentary directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim; Sundance winner To Hold a Mountain , directed by Biljana Tutorov and Petar Glomazić, and Once Upon a Time in Harlem , directed by David Greaves. Two films centered on Gaza also made the short list: American Doctor , directed by Poh Si Teng, and NAZA , directed by Oscar winners Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor.

Related Stories

'Ashland' Trailer: First Look At Wyatt Maw's Debut Feature Ahead Of DOC NYC

DOC NYC Set To Honor Documentary Visionaries Alex Gibney, JT Takagi, Stephen Maing, And Raney Aronson-Rath

Scroll for the complete list of films to make the DOC NYC short lists for features and shorts. DOC NYC also announced films its Winner’s Circle and Selects Encore sections, completing the 2026 program. The festival runs in person from November 11-19 at IFC Center, SVA Theatre, and Village East by Angelika in New York City; it continues online through November 29 (with films available to viewers across the U.S.).

Watch on Deadline

DOC NYC’s Short List: Features selection committee is overseen by Artistic Director Jaie Laplante and Director of Special Projects Thom Powers.

“The Short Lists sections showcase a selection of nonfiction features and shorts that the festival’s programming team considers to be among the year’s strongest contenders for Oscars and other prizes,” notes a release, “while Winner’s Circle is a celebration of films already awarded at major international and U.S. film events that are worthy of additional consideration. Selects Encore showcases significant titles from DOC NYC’s year-round Selects screening series—films that continue to be part of our awards season conversations.”

Winner’s Circle screenings include the NYC premiere of Pegah Ahangarani’s Rehearsals for a Revolution — winner of the L’Œeil d’Or prize for Best Documentary at Cannes and the UK submission for Best International Feature Film at the Oscars – and Closure , Michał Marczak’s documentary that won the Golden Alexander at the Thessaloniki International Documentary Festival in Greece.

Among short documentaries making DOC NYC’s short list: The Baddest Speech Writer of All , directed by two-time Oscar winner Ben Proudfoot and NBA great Stephen Curry; The Boys and the Bees , directed by Arielle Knight; La Tierra del Valor (Home of the Brave) , directed by Cristina Costantini; They’re Here , directed by Laura Poitras and Rachel Lauren Mueller; The Revolution Against Death , directed by Joshua Oppenheimer; The Tuners , directed by Pawel Piotr Chorzepa, and Water Cooler , directed by Emma V.F.

This year’s selections for Short List: Features are:

14TH

Director: Ava DuVernay; Producers: Ava DuVernay, Spencer Averick, Tammy Garnes, Paul Garnes

A powerful film essay exploring the legacy of the 14th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution.

AMERICAN DOCTOR

Director: Poh Si Teng; Producers: Poh Si Teng, Kirstine Barfod, Reem Haddad

A visceral, unflinching film following three notable U.S. physicians as they provide in-person support at a Gaza hospital treating victims of mass-casualty events from the Israeli war campaign.

THE BEND IN THE RIVER

Director: Robb Moss; Producers: Lisa Remington, Kristin Feeley

A masterful meditation on the eternal, the temporal and the inevitable, from veteran filmmaker Robb Moss.

EVERYBODY TO KENMURE STREET

Director: Felipe Bustos Sierra; Producer: Ciara Barry

An uplifting portrayal of resistance focuses on an incident in 2021 when immigration officers conducted a raid on Glasgow’s Kenmure Street.

A FOX UNDER A PINK MOON (NYC Premiere)

Directors: Mehrdad Oskouei, Soraya Akhlaghi; Producer: Mehrdad Oskouei

A young, talented Afghan woman living under the thumb of the patriarchy in Iran channels her emotions into unforgettable expressions of art.

THE GREAT EXPERIMENT

Directors: Stephen Maing, Eric Daniel Metzgar; Producers: Stephen Maing, Eric Daniel Metzgar, Farihah Zaman

Traversing the U.S. from 2016 to 2020, patient observational filmmaking becomes a temperature check on American democracy—what George Washington described as the last great experiment in promoting human happiness in civil society. Co-director Stephen Maing will receive the Robert and Anne Drew Award for Documentary Excellence at this year’s DOC NYC Visionaries Tribute.

MUSK

Director: Alex Gibney; Producers: Alex Gibney, Jessie Deeter, Erin Edeiken, Zhang Xin, Joey Marra, Nick Shumaker, Jessica Grimshaw, Dana O’Keefe

An epic work profiling the world’s first trillionaire, Elon Musk. Director Alex Gibney will receive the Lifetime Achievement Award at this year’s DOC NYC Visionaries Tribute.

NAZA

Directors: Yuval Abraham, Rachel Szor; Producers: Harry Davies, Lindsay Poulton, James Wilson

Anonymous members of the Israel Defense Force candidly reflect on their attitudes toward civilian casualties, known as NAZA, and how they process the meaning of genocide.

ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM

Director: David Greaves; Producers: Liani Greaves, Anne de Mare

A glorious night, capturing a vital period of American culture, when luminaries who had been active in the Harlem Renaissance of the 1920s recount their memories.

ONE IN A MILLION

Directors: Itab Azzam, Jack MacInnes; Producers: Will Anderson, James Bluemel, Andrew Palmer, Raney Aronson-Rath

A chronicle of one Syrian daughter’s journey in fleeing war and seeking refuge in Germany, and how over ten years, new pressures and opportunities present themselves.

SOUL PATROL

Director: J.M. Harper; Producers: Sam Bisbee, Danielle Massie, J.M. Harper, Nasir Jones, Peter Bittenbender

A hidden chapter of American military history—the Vietnam War’s first Black special ops team, an elite unit operating deep behind enemy lines.

TIME AND WATER

Director: Sara Dosa; Producers: Shane Boris, Elijah Stevens, Jameka Autry, Sara Dosa

A letter to the next generation by an Icelandic poet, reflecting on the melting glaciers that are a harbinger of climate change.

TO HOLD A MOUNTAIN (NYC Premiere)

Directors: Biljana Tutorov, Petar Glomazić; Producers: Biljana Tutorov, Petar Glomazić, Quentin Laurent, Rok Biček

In the remote highlands of Montenegro, the spirit of motherhood, the violence of men, and the sacredness of the mountain collide and reconcile.

WILD INSIDE

Director: Penny Lane; Producers: Gabriel Sedgwick, Nickolas Hasse

In 2023, Flaco the Eurasian Eagle Owl became an international folk hero and a mythological figure for a world in which so many find themselves living in circumstances far away from their roots.

YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING

Directors: Nathan Fielder, Lance Oppenheim; Producers: Nathan Fielder, Lance Oppenheim, Tatiana Bears, Maggie Ambrose, Jack Davis

As she prepares to begin serving her federal prison sentence, disgraced Silicon Valley tycoon Elizabeth Holmes continues to claim she has never lied, as America’s premiere absurdist documentarians record her every word.

SHORT LIST: SHORTS

The Short List: Shorts showcase of 15 titles is now in its ninth year at DOC NYC. The selection process is overseen by Artistic Director Jaie Laplante, Director of Special Projects Thom Powers, and consultant Samah Ali. In 2025, the showcase included All The Empty Rooms, which went on to win the Oscar.

This year’s selections for Short List: Shorts are:

THE BADDEST SPEECHWRITER OF ALL

Directors: Ben Proudfoot, Stephen Curry; Producers: Stephen Curry, Erick Peyton, Ben Proudfoot

At 93, Martin Luther King Jr. ‘s lawyer and speechwriter offers a living testament to history, and reminds us that silence is still our most urgent problem.

THE BOYS AND THE BEES

Director: Arielle Knight; Producer: Sean Weiner

On an idyllic farm in rural Georgia, beekeeping parents tenderly share their knowledge of life, love, and nature with their young sons while restoring their homestead.

BUCKSKIN

Director/Producer: Mars Verrone

A ground-breaking African-American and indigenous forester reflects on his life’s work of conservation and ancestral knowledge, while he approaches the twilight of his days.

A DERAILMENT

Director: Nathan Truesdell; Producers: Kat Nguyen, Will Lennon

A 2023 freight train derailment in rural Ohio corporate gives rise to a shocking new low in corporate maleficence.

THE GRANDFATHER PUZZLE

Director: Ora DeKornfeld; Producers: Zsofia Paczolay, Noémi Veronika Szakonyi, Máté Artur Vincze

Ora wants to better understand her aging grandfather before it’s too late. When she travels to Hungary to see if she can unlock the mysteries of his defense mechanisms, she finds a world left behind that illuminates a deep appreciation for life as it is now.

LA TIERRA DEL VALOR (THE HOME OF THE BRAVE)

Director: Cristina Costantini; Producers: Cristina Costantini, Alfie Koetter

In the face of growing antipathy towards immigrants, Latina pop star NEZZA makes the bold choice to perform the National Anthem at Dodger Stadium in Spanish, sparking an outpouring of outrage, support, and discussion about freedom of speech and who decides what ‘American’ means.

LISTEN

Director: Taliesin Black-Brown; Producers: Taliesin Black-Brown, Sam Davis, Greg Moga

An Alaskan sound specialist works for preservation within two levels of loss – the fading songs of wildlife disappearing from the wilderness, as climate change threatens natural populations; and his mother’s disappearing memory, as she slowly succumbs to dementia.

THE OATH

Directors: Liane Aviram, Louis Hollis; Producer: Liane Aviram

Dr Lina Qasem-Hassan, a Palestinian living and working in Israel, teaches medical ethics as well as practising as a physician – walking a tightrope of activism and professionalism while working through the trauma of her people.

ONE LAST ORDER

Directors: Lauren Defilippo, Sam Soko; Producers: Lauren Defilippo, Sam Soko, Amanda Pollak

After 37 years at Mac’s Drive-Thru in Gainesville, Florida, sunny and beloved Sighle is retiring. As customers travel from near and far to say goodbye, this heartwarming portrait celebrates an everyday worker who always went above and beyond, and the joy and community one person can inspire.

AN OPEN FIELD

Director: Teboho Edkins; Producers: Don Edkins, Carine Chichkowsky

One hundred and fifty seven people died when a new Boeing 737 MAX crashed in Ethiopia in 2019. While Boeing callously deflects blame for their negligence, a family of one victim finds strength in gathering collective mourning.

OUTPOSTS – NOTHING HERE IS YOURS

Director: Hilla Medalia; Producers: Hilla Medalia, Sheila Nevins, Yael Melamed

In the West Bank, Palestinian shepherd communities face escalating settler violence and displacement, while a group of Israeli activists stand in solidarity with shepherd communities as they struggle to remain on their land.

THE REVOLUTION AGAINST DEATH

Director: Joshua Oppenheimer; Producer: Signe Byrge Sørensen

A sharp, provocative look at the anti-aging industry and our increasingly elaborate efforts to resist mortality.

THEY’RE HERE

Directors: Laura Poitras, Rachel Lauren Mueller; Producers: Rachel Lauren Mueller, Laura Poitras, Yoni Golijov

A view of the evils of ICE through an organized resistance group of citizens in Minneapolis during the 2025-26 winter, using a unique cinematic language.

THE TUNERS

Director: Pawel Piotr Chorzepa; Producer: Joanna Chorzepa

Behind the scenes of Warsaw’s Chopin Festival, a group of expert tuners vie to achieve the perfect pitch so that the champion pianist will win on their instrument.

WATER COOLER

Director/Producer: Emma V.F.

In the halls of NYC’s immigration court, the casual chitchat of ICE agents waiting to arrest their unsuspecting targets stands in stark contrast to the horrors these detainees are likely to face.

WINNER’S CIRCLE

The DOC NYC Winner’s Circle for documentary features, introduced in 2019, highlights films that arrive at DOC NYC with significant awards pedigrees already in place. Past films shown in Winner’s Circle that all went on to further acclaim include Writing with Fire, The Mole Agent, A House Made of Splinters, Hollywoodgate, In the Rearview, Bad Axe, Midnight Family, and Advocate. To qualify for inclusion in this category, films must have won a major award at a significant international or US film festival.

This year’s selections for Winner’s Circle are:

AMERICAN PACHUCO: THE LEGEND OF LUIS VALDEZ

Director: David Alvarado; Producers: David Alvarado, Lauren DeFilippo, Everett Katigbak, Amanda Pollak

Against political resistance and industry skepticism, Luis Valdez pushes Chicano storytelling forward, creating iconic works that challenge, celebrate, and expand America’s story. Winner, Audience Award: U.S. Documentary and Festival Favorite Award, 2026 Sundance Film Festival

BUCKS HARBOR

Director: Pete Muller; Producers: Pete Muller, Nathan Golon, Noel Paul

Striking cinematography marks this observant, verite film about men in East Maine, the traditions of their elders, and their complex inner lives. Winner, Golden Eye Award for Best Documentary Film, 2026 Zurich Film Festival

CLOSURE

Director: Michał Marczak; Producers: Monika Braid, Rémi Grellety, Michał Marczak, Katarzyna Szczerba, Karolina Marczak

A haunting portrait of what it means to seek closure that’s a testament to parental love. Winner, Golden Alexander International Competition Award, 2026 Thessaloniki International Documentary Festival

AN EYE FOR AN EYE

Directors: Tanaz Eshaghian, Farzad Jafari; Producers: Christoph Jorg, Katayoon Arsanjani, Gelareh Kiazand, Joey Marra

A tense examination of Iran’s justice system and one family torn asunder by a legacy of abuse and mariticide, unfolding like a Shakespearean tragedy. Winner, Grand Prize Impact Documentary, 2026 Fipadoc

GIVE ME THE BALL!

Directors: Liz Garbus, Elizabeth Wolff; Producers: Liz Garbus, Elizabeth Wolff, Chris James, Dan Cogan, Dominic Crossley-Holland, Gentry Kirby

Billie Jean King, the iconic athlete who changed both the worlds of tennis and of women’s athletics, offers new perspectives on her legacy and the state of the sports world. Winner, Audience Award / Best Documentary Feature, 2026 Provincetown International Film Festival

NUISANCE BEAR

Directors: Gabriela Osio Vanden, Jack Weisman; Producers: Will N. Miller, Michael Code, Teddy Leifer, Jack Weisman, Gabriela Osio Vanden

The modern clash between human beings and polar bears takes on an ironic meaning when an Inuit elder shares his perspectives on the ancient belief and customs of his people. Winner, U.S. Documentary: Grand Jury Prize, 2026 Sundance Film Festival

REHEARSALS FOR A REVOLUTION (NYC Premiere)

Director: Pegah Ahangarani; Producers: Parnian Farnam, Pegah Ahangarani, Arash Ashtiani

Celebrated Iranian actor Pegah Ahangarani creates an essayistic documentary, weaving together home movies and news broadcasts to construct a vivid portrait of Iran’s modern history in the four decades since the revolution. Winner, L’Œil d’or Documentary Award, 2026 Cannes Film Festival

STEAL THIS STORY, PLEASE!

Directors: Carl Deal, Tia Lessin; Producers: Carl Deal, Tia Lessin, Karen Ranucci, Diana Cohn, Caren Spruch

Amy Goodman of Democracy Now! pursues the news with integrity and dauntlessness, seeing independent journalism as a major force for good. Winner, Greg Gund Memorial Standing Up Competition, Cleveland International Film Festival; Santa Barbara International Film Festival, Social Justice Award Winner; audience awards at Santa Barbara International Film Festival 2025; Mill Valley Film Festival 2025; Woodstock Film Festival 2025, SIFF DocFest 2025; Palm Springs International Film Festival 2026; St. Louis International Film Festival 2025, and more.

SELECTS ENCORE

Selects Encore showcases a selection of films that screened at DOC NYC Selects, the festival’s ongoing screening series extension that runs annually from late winter through summer. The films chosen for Selects Encore represent works that continue to be present in the season’s awards conversations.

This year’s selections for Selects Encore are:

DAYLIGHT

Director: Jon Kasbe; Producers: Jon Kasbe, Zoe Rogovin

Serving a life sentence for murder, Joe Garcia finds unexpected refuge in Taylor Swift’s lyrics. When an essay he writes about love and music goes viral, it cracks open the past and rekindles a connection, opening the door to a life and love he thought were lost forever.

A LIFE ILLUMINATED

Director: Tasha Van Zandt; Producers: Tasha Van Zandt, Sebastian Zeck, Jessica Harrop, Kathryn Everett

A daring quest to document a bioluminescent phenomenon that could forever change how we understand life on Earth.

MANHOOD

Director: Daniel Lombroso; Producers: Kerry Mack, Rebecca Shaid

Manhood explores shame, sex, and the fragile myths of American masculinity, with dark humor and unexpected empathy.

MARY OLIVER: SAVED BY THE BEAUTY OF THE WORLD

Director/Producer: Sasha Waters

If poetry had a pop icon, Mary Oliver would be it, and Sasha Waters’ beguiling portrait is as poetic as its protagonist.

SCENES FROM THE DIVIDE

Director: Alison Klayman; Producers: Alison Klayman, Courtney Powell

A fierce battle among American Jews over identity, history, and responsibility is revealed in the homes of New Yorkers on both sides of Zohran Mamdani’s 2025 mayoral campaign.

THEYDREAM

Director: William D. Caballero; Producers: William D. Caballero, Brad Jones, Erin Ploss-Campoamor, Elaine Del Valle

A deeply personal documentary that examines the transformative nature of grief for a close-knit Puerto Rican family.

WHO MOVES AMERICA

Director: Yael Bridge; Producers: Yael Bridge, Jeremy Flood, Yoni Golijov, Mars Verrone

Examines the tense 2023 contract negotiations between UPS and its 340,000 unionized workers, as a microcosm for the larger struggles of labor justice in the U.S.A.

"参展作家包括厚川文子、五十岚裕贵、内田悠、川地彩香、杉田明彦、染谷聪、辻野刚、富井贵志、中里隆、古谷宣幸、古谷朱里等。活动将介绍陶艺、木工、漆艺、玻璃、和纸、染织等多领域作品，同时特别展出黑田辰秋、河井宽次郎、Bernard Leach、西村圭功等近代工艺名品。由此浮现从过去延续至现在的日本工艺谱系。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外，以冲绳为据点的草木染作家kitta的装置作品《Yellow Scalle》也将展出。作品在户外展示以当地植物的枝叶、树皮、根等染制的布料，呈现工艺作为自然与人之间媒介的形态。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外还将举行6场对谈。10月17日，独立研究者森田真生与和纸作家谷口弦将登台，参与思考自然环境与造物关系的“森林、水与工艺”。随后，律师小松隼也与木工家富井贵志将讨论工艺的品牌化与海外拓展。接着，日本美术史家Timon Screech与高桥伸城将解读从本阿弥光悦到琳派的日本美术谱系。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "18日，随笔作家内田也哉子与しょうざんリゾート京都的松山佳世将围绕手工艺与日常生活的关係展开对谈。演员井浦新将与冲绳木地师渡庆次弘幸一同登台，以“从土地诞生之物”为主题。在鹿儿岛培育植物、以天然香料制作产品的井浦，与活用冲绳树木制作漆器的渡庆次，将围绕素材、土地风土以及自然与人的关系展开对话。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此外，编辑若林惠与Kokuyo横库研究所所长山下正太郎将在“社会工艺的时代”中，考察个人作家的作品与手工艺在全世界受到关注的背景。并随当代社会的变化，探讨工艺的价值如何被发现、评价与流通。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "实际使用、品味工艺的节目也很充实。作为对本阿弥光悦的致敬，将与淡交社合作举办特别茶会“光悦憧憬”。此外，还准备了特别晚餐：由陶艺家中里隆监修，古谷宣幸与古谷朱里用鹰峯的土制作器皿，盛装京都“御膳宫泽”的料理。还将举办接触和蜡烛与烛台、炼香与香炉、和果子与木箱、竹细工等各种素材与技法的工作坊。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不只隔着展示柜欣赏工艺，而是在巡游历史建筑与庭园的同时接触作品，与创作者对话，并通过饮食与茶来体验。这将是从光悦昔日构筑艺术村的鹰峯出发、追问工艺新价值的2天。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "text": "また、沖縄を拠点とする草木染め作家kittaによるインスタレーション《Yellow Scalle》も展開。土地の植物の枝葉や樹皮、根などで染めた布を屋外に展示し、自然と人間を媒介する工芸のあり方を提示する。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "また6回のトークセッションを実施。10月17日には、独立研究者の森田真生と和紙作家の谷口弦が、自然環境とものづくりの関係を考える「森と水と工芸」に登壇。続いて、弁護士の小松隼也と木工家の富井貴志が、工芸のブランディングや海外展開について議論する。さらに、日本美術史家のタイモン・スクリーチと高橋伸城が、本阿弥光悦から琳派へとつながる日本美術の系譜を読み解く。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "工芸を実際に使い、味わうプログラムも充実する。本阿弥光悦へのオマージュとして、淡交社との協働による特別茶会「光悦憧憬」を開催。さらに、陶芸家・中里隆が監修し、古谷宣幸と古谷朱里が鷹峯の土を用いて制作した器で、京都の「ごだん宮ざわ」の料理を味わう特別ディナーも用意される。和蝋燭と燭台、練り香と香炉、和菓子と木箱、竹細工など、さまざまな素材と技法に触れるワークショップも実施する。"}, article_text:
陶芸、木工、漆芸、金工など、約30組の現代工芸作家が集結する新たな文化イベント「MOSS KOGEI Kyoto 2026」が、2026年10月17日（土）・18日（日）の2日間、京都・鷹峯のしょうざんリゾート京都で初開催される。「これからの用の美」をテーマに、工芸作品の展示・販売をはじめ、茶会、食、ワークショップ、トークセッションなどを通して、現代における工芸の可能性を探る。

会場となる鷹峯は、江戸初期に本阿弥光悦が芸術村を築いた土地として知られる。書や陶芸、漆芸、蒔絵、茶の湯など、異なる領域の職人や芸術家たちが集い、創造を育んだ場所だ。本イベントでは、その精神を現代に受け継ぎ、工芸を伝統技術としてだけでなく、人と自然、暮らし、社会を結ぶ思想として捉え直す。

会場のしょうざんリゾート京都には、約3万5000坪の敷地に苔の日本庭園や数寄屋建築、茶室が点在。明治期に裏千家11世玄々斎が建てた茶室「聴松庵」、日本画家・榊原紫峰の旧邸「紫峰邸」、円山応挙らによる襖絵を有する「峰玉亭」など、歴史的な建築空間を舞台に作品が展示される。

出展作家には、厚川文子、五十嵐裕貴、内田悠、川地あや香、杉田明彦、染谷聡、辻野剛、富井貴志、中里隆、古谷宣幸、古谷朱里らが名を連ねる。陶芸や木工、漆芸、ガラス、和紙、染織など多様な分野の作品を紹介するとともに、黒田辰秋、河井寬次郎、バーナード・リーチ、西村圭功ら近代工芸の名品も特別展示。過去から現在へと連なる日本の工芸の系譜を浮かび上がらせる。

また、沖縄を拠点とする草木染め作家kittaによるインスタレーション《Yellow Scalle》も展開。土地の植物の枝葉や樹皮、根などで染めた布を屋外に展示し、自然と人間を媒介する工芸のあり方を提示する。

また6回のトークセッションを実施。10月17日には、独立研究者の森田真生と和紙作家の谷口弦が、自然環境とものづくりの関係を考える「森と水と工芸」に登壇。続いて、弁護士の小松隼也と木工家の富井貴志が、工芸のブランディングや海外展開について議論する。さらに、日本美術史家のタイモン・スクリーチと高橋伸城が、本阿弥光悦から琳派へとつながる日本美術の系譜を読み解く。

18日には、エッセイストの内田也哉子と、しょうざんリゾート京都の松山佳世が、手仕事と日々の暮らしの関係を語り合う。俳優の井浦新は、沖縄の木地師・渡慶次弘幸とともに「土地から生まれるもの」をテーマに登壇。鹿児島で植物を育て、天然香料を用いたプロダクトを手がける井浦と、沖縄の木々を生かして漆器を制作する渡慶次が、素材や土地の風土、自然と人間の関係について対話する。

また、編集者の若林恵とコクヨ ヨコク研究所所長の山下正太郎による「ソーシャル工芸の時代」では、個人作家の作品や手仕事が世界各地で注目を集める背景を考察。工芸の価値がどのように発見され、評価され、流通していくのかを、現代社会の変化とともに探る。

工芸を実際に使い、味わうプログラムも充実する。本阿弥光悦へのオマージュとして、淡交社との協働による特別茶会「光悦憧憬」を開催。さらに、陶芸家・中里隆が監修し、古谷宣幸と古谷朱里が鷹峯の土を用いて制作した器で、京都の「ごだん宮ざわ」の料理を味わう特別ディナーも用意される。和蝋燭と燭台、練り香と香炉、和菓子と木箱、竹細工など、さまざまな素材と技法に触れるワークショップも実施する。

工芸を展示ケースの中だけで鑑賞するのではなく、歴史ある建築や庭園を巡りながら、作品に触れ、作り手と対話し、食や茶を通して体験する。光悦がかつて芸術村を築いた鷹峯から、工芸の新たな価値を問いかける2日間となる。

Editor’s note: T his story contains details of alleged sexual offenses that some readers may find distressing .

An indecent assault charge against Russell Brand has been reduced as the prosecution wraps its case at London’s Southwark Crown Court.

The judge told jurors there was “insufficient evidence” for the charge and it has instead been reduced to attempted indecent assault. The jury went through the formalities of finding Brand not guilty on the now-replaced charge. There are six other charges.

The charge concerned complainant 2 in the Brand trial – who we are calling C2 as she has a lifelong right to anonymity – who said that she was working for MTV in London at the time and had been showing him where the toilets were when he attempted to pull her into the bathroom. “I said, ‘What are you doing? Are you mad? Let me go’, and then he started to plead almost, saying, ‘Go on, go on, come in’,” she told the court 11 days ago.

Watch on Deadline

Related Stories

Russell Brand's Former Assistant Claims Women Came To Comedian's Flat For Sex All The Time But He "Never Seemed Happy" Afterwards

Chris Brown Given Suspended Prison Sentence For London Nightclub Confrontation

Brand had sex “in countless locations and scenarios”

The judge reduced the charge on the final full day of the prosecution’s case, although a few loose ends will be wrapped up tomorrow morning.

Before the charge was reduced, the court heard several statements Brand made at the start of four different police interviews from between 2023 and 2025 about the allegations, during which he repeatedly denied all charges while saying he “had sexual encounters in countless locations and scenarios, often with people I had just met.”

Brand faces three charges of rape, three counts of sexual assault and now one of attempted indecent assault based on allegations made by six women . His team will set out his defense from tomorrow, and he denies all charges and has pleaded not guilty. Deadline has been reporting daily from a live video feed of the courtroom since the trial began.

Brand, who could take the stand tomorrow, used these pre-prepared statements to police to say he “led a very promiscuous life, which I have spent years openly denouncing.” He slammed the 2023 Channel 4 documentary and The Times report about the allegations as “defamatory” and “fictitious,” which he said had “invited additional allegations to be made” that were “invented or reimagined.” “The magnitude of promiscuity deceptively rendered in recent media attacks have caused consensual encounters to be reframed decades later,” Brand told police.

Brand said he “did not recall the names of the complainants or meeting them,” but added it is “entirely possible that I may have encountered them and we my have engaged in consensual sexual activity that has since been reimagined.”

“I have had consensual sex in toilet cubicles at parties but have never forced anyone into a toilet or forced my penis into anyone’s mouth,” he said in one statement responding to an allegation from complainant C3 in the trial, who alleges she was orally raped by Brand.

In a different police interview, the court heard that Brand said he “had sexual encounters in countless locations and scenarios, often with people I had just met,” but again stressed that these were all consensual.

“At live shows, press events and junkets I did my best to be accessible, non-discriminatory and loving,” he told police. “I spent lots of time at these events. I have shared kisses with hundreds of members of the public during these events and hundreds of photos are available online. Everything I did in public could be photographed once I was famous and could end up in the tabloids. I was aware of this. I routinely made provocative jokes or comments both with members of the public and during live performances and broadcasts.”

At the end of each of these pre-prepared statements to police, the court heard how Brand said he did not intend to respond to any police questions “without sufficient time to consider the information to answer accurately.”

Brand could take the stand tomorrow as his defense begins. This is anticipated to last another two to three weeks.

The trial continues.

article_text:
一般財団法人未来文化創造財団は、文化が持続的に発展する社会基盤づくりの活動のひとつとして、京都御所の西南に タイム堂ギャラリー をオープンする。こけら落としとして、 「森万里子：Shrine II ─ 内なる光のトポロジー」 を開催。会期は11月6日から2027年3月31日まで。

森万里子 は、人類と宇宙との関係を考察する作品で知られる、多分野にわたるアーティスト。大規模なパブリックアートでは、精神性の探究と未来的な美学を融合させ、自然、人類、テクノロジーが調和する関係性を描き出してきた。

本展は、現代社会における分断と不安のなかで私たちが抱える「個」という孤独に焦点を当てる。森は、自らが体験した圧倒的な光の記憶──あらゆる次元へと広がる、生命根源の無限の愛の出現──を通して、人類が本来つながっているはずの宇宙的全一性を呼び覚ます。森が提示する「聖域」は、たんなる日常からの逃避ではなく、私たち一人ひとりの内にある静かな光へと立ち返り、魂の永遠の絆を再発見するための試みだ。

空間の中核をなす立体インスタレーションと、壁面を囲む平面作品で構成される本展は、作品群の共鳴によって、ギャラリー全体をひとつの「知覚の装置（アパラタス）」へと変容させる。

立体インスタレーション《Shrine II》は、春日大社摂社・水谷神社の床下に鎮座する聖なる磐座（いわくら）へのオマージュ。重層的にレイアウトされた几帳の中心に、クリスタル製の磐座が据えられる。奈良時代以来、龍神信仰の霊地として崇められてきた水谷川の聖性をタイム堂の空間へと転移させ、自己と世界を静かにつなぎ直す親密な体験として立ち上がる。

空間の周囲には、8点の掛け軸が展観される。平安古筆の息づかいに身を委ね、森自身が体験した光の記憶が描かれている。本シリーズは、意味を伝達する情報記号としての文字ではなく、生命の脈動を宿した形而上学的な「持続（Durée）」へと還流させる試みだ。

本ギャラリーは、京都御所の南西角に建つ大正期の町家二棟を結び、ひとつのギャラリーへとリノベーションされたもの。新たな文化的価値を育み、次の創造へとつなぐ場の幕開けとなる本展に注目したい。なお、10月31日より 森美術館 では 「森万里子：燦燦」 が開催される。ぜひ合わせて見てほしい。

article_text:
Dame Judi Dench has long made her feelings clear about Cats, the doomed 2019 adaptation of the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical. In an interview the year after release, she said she had so far declined to watch the movie – in which she played wise moggy Old Deuteronomy – and described the orange fur coat she had to wear as looking like “five foxes fucking on my back”.

In her forthcoming memoir, Is It Too Late to Make a Run for It? Dench reflects further on her involvement in the movie, which was universally panned and whose director, Tom Hooper , has not made a film since.

“Oh God, I can’t bear it,” she writes in the book, “and [Lloyd Webber] had waited so long for it to be made. What a waste of all that goodwill and talent.

“I understand the critics were rather hostile to the film. I never saw the final cut so I can’t judge. All I’ll say is nobody sets out to give a poor performance or make a bad film. You do your best, offer something up and hope that people will get on board and join the party.”

Among the aspects of the film most energetically criticised on release was the film’s erratic CGI, which erased every animal’s anus but retained, in the case of Dench, a human hand, complete with wedding ring.

In her book, Dench writes that she felt “ill at ease from the beginning – I just didn’t feel right in the role”. Nor, she continues, did she “like the way the young dancers were left hanging at the end of each take. They’d stand there exhausted and be completely ignored.”

However, Dench says she did enjoy discovering “I could still lift my leg in the air” and playing Bananagrams with her vocal coach on set. She also liked meeting co-star Taylor Swift and, on the final day of filming, was given 50 everlasting roses, spraypainted gold, by Jason Derulo, who played Rum Tum Tugger.

“There were no villains in the making of Cats ,” writes Dench. “And if something isn’t a success, then there are always things you can say you’ve learned.

“Sometimes things just don’t work out: the timing’s wrong, the cast don’t gel, the elements don’t coalesce. But people’s intentions are mostly honourable.”

Lloyd Webber has vociferously criticised the film, saying Hooper did not consult those involved in the original West End show and saying “the whole thing was ridiculous”.

In 2021, he called it “off-the-scale all wrong” and said the experience left him so “emotionally damaged” he became a dog owner in an effort to recover.

“There wasn’t really any understanding of why the music ticked at all. I saw it and I just thought, ‘Oh, God, no.’ It was the first time in my 70-odd years on this planet that I went out and bought a dog. So the one good thing to come out of it is my little Havanese puppy.”

The composer said that he had to prove to an airline that he required the companion as an emotional support animal in order to travel with him. “I said: ‘Just see what Hollywood did to my musical Cats.’ Then the approval came back with a note saying, ‘No doctor’s report required.’”

"到处都是图像。照片、照片的照片、照片的模仿、非照片、肖像、自拍、裸照、静物、花瓶、风景、橱窗、人类的多样性、民主的森林、连续且相同的城市、从一个机场到另一个机场漫无边际的迪士尼乐园-体育馆，这就是当下。无论“自我”究竟为何，在今天（但“今天”是在哪个经度？），它都属于行程错误的范畴，属于被遗忘在转盘上传送带上、让我们误了转机航班的行李，然而，已经没有人会从地图（从图像）中迷失，正如森山大道所说，所有的狗都是家养的狗；我们所有人也都去图片库度过假。孩子们生来就是另一个物种的人类，面对一个充满照片杂音、视频超级丰富、雄性全景、谷歌地图化的星球；他们已经在深度伪造——人工智能——戏剧性与摆拍——隐私之死亡的认识论中成形——上帝知道这个定时炸弹会带来什么——一切都永远改变了，却又什么都没有赢得，或者更确切地说，一切都原封不动甚至变得更糟，因此，最好的尚未到来，我们面前拥有一切：战争、地震、分裂、数据中心——那是最好的时代，那是最坏的时代；当我们死去时，我们都会去云端。我们会为家庭相册和我们没有生下的孩子哭泣，真想买个农场，做陶瓷，用图像过上阿米什人的生活，只给朋友写信，永远读书。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "无论“自我”是什么，对大多数人来说，今天它意味着别的东西。介于“无人机”和“杜阿·利帕”（Dua Lipa）之间。看到一个年轻的YouTube博主拍下自己盯着一面空墙看一小时以“最大化”其能力的视频，人们会笑出声来。“这就是我，”他一脸严肃地说，“不看图像，不看YouTube，不与社交媒体互动。”我发布，故我在。大步向前的年轻人（朝着什么方向？），发生的一切都指向汇入一个动态信息流，而在精英文学院里，富人的孩子们加入了新的勒德分子俱乐部，用不了多久，那里就会有晚宴、狂欢教派、集体自杀、大规模枪击事件。而一群记者则会像往常一样姗姗来迟，带着惊愕、震惊和警报，随后将是一片恐慌、各种文章、激烈的辩论和声援音乐会。而在他们不在的地方，在公共和私人领域，则会孕育出希望的萌芽。微小的匿名姿态、没有交易的相互帮助、没有算法的分享、陌生人之间的仁慈、暮色下身体的美丽，会有万寿菊和无花果树、欢笑、冷饮、摆好的餐桌、远方朋友迟来的午餐——而且还会有图像。当看到美与优雅时，仍会有人把手伸向笔记本去画点什么。一句诗，一条手臂，一棵树，一座房子。会有蚂蚁，因为会有剩饭剩菜、面包屑、水果核。既然有了照相机，就会产生一种冲动，正如约翰·伯格（John Berger）所说，要让这种姿态变得“对自身有意识”。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2.", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "图像的超饱和、那种痛苦的感知——即“现实[变得]像一张巨大的照片或蒙太奇”（路易吉·吉里《全集》，65页）——以及对其“超精确度”（72页）的焦虑（尽管只是少数人的焦虑），让人担忧这种冲动会灭绝。人们担心，视觉过量一方面会导致凝固的麻木，另一方面会由于普遍且不可逆地放弃外部性而导致精神的迟钝。当“如果我们还愿意给它这个名字的话”摄影不再依赖相机时，随之而来的将是对生活表面那种迷人关系的压制，相机本是这种关系工具和借口，这种关系与其说是绘画不如说是舞蹈，与其说是电影和戏剧不如说是文学和自传。所有这一切以及住房成本，导致了摄影忧郁和悲观主义的模式，将我们引向沉默和消逝：引向对一种切实意义的希望，它位于中心之外，背对“时事”，且与权力和“未来”无法调和。这并非怀旧，而是一种抵抗，预计它将绽放出本十年、本世纪前半叶最挽歌式的摄影反思，它们将作为同情的时刻，姗姗来迟地进入画廊和博物馆。摄影或许将就此终结。作为我们所知的摄影。它将作为档案、图书馆、遗产、有日期的过程、乐谱、玩具继续存在。在高级订阅中，将会有算法生成的虚拟回顾展。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "像伟大的加泰罗尼亚艺术家琼·丰库贝塔（Joan Fontcuberta）这样的乐观主义者，将这一可能的结果（既然墨菲定律似乎已经成了数学规律，这便是可能的）——即消除作为“使观察实现自我意识的过程”的摄影（贝尔杰，《理解摄影》，38）——视为一个逻辑且幸福的结局。我们终将从“摄影旧政权及其指称的暴政”中解放出来（《反对巴特》，130）。因为“指称的暴政”除了正如波德莱尔所写的那样，“un moi insatiable du non-moi”（“一个对非我不知餍足的我”）之外，还能假设什么呢？——一个被这样一种冲动奴役的我：渴望将观察、以及它对光线如何在时空间的一片切片中绘制可见之物之反应镌刻下来。暴政归暴政，新政权将是技术浪漫主义的：直接摄影的终结将标志着艺术的内向投射、非指称性、这个不知餍足的自我的自我 apotheosis（神化），顺便说一句，它与时代精神（Zeitgeist）很合拍。然而，有以下细微差别。“摄影”将不再是自然的镜子（如果它曾经是的话），但——瓦吉尼亚·伍尔夫请解惑，萨尔科夫斯基请解惑——它也不会是内省的反映。它将不再是一扇通往世界的窗户，而将变成一扇通往（艺术家的灵魂？主观想象？——哦，不，千万别是这个）非人类反刍视觉回应的窗户，这些回应是针对对经过逐步开发迭代的专业软件所提出之阐述的。（显然，这是通过包月或包年套餐订阅的，学生还有特别优惠，在黑色星期五和网络星期一等日子里打折，直到你需要升级你的内存空间。）尼埃普斯心里想的肯定不是这个，但你们拿去吧。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们无意以不应有的轻率态度来抹杀丰库贝塔一书真正的敏锐性与原创性。他对巴特的论战（出乎所有人意料，它本也可以被称为《反对迈克尔·弗雷德》Against Michael Fried）在其他方面具有深刻、尖锐且顺便说一句十分滑稽的维度。尽管他对巴特充满了不耐烦，但他对《明室》的分析——特别是“Barthology”那一章——却是详尽、全面且严谨的。然而，这既不是对这本过去十年中出现的关于摄影的最具启发性的著作进行深入批评评介的恰当场合，也不是合适的语境。他对罗兰·巴特那些已沦为批评陈词滥调的直觉的修正（很想说：拆解）——例如关于 studium 和 punctum 著名区分的条款与内涵，或者摄影所能表达的极限莫过于“ça-a-été”、“这曾发生过”的想法，以及巴特在面对不一致性时带着明显冷漠而不断兜售的其他观念（迈克尔·弗雷德也曾以一种诱人的柔和指出过这一点，他将巴特招募到了弗雷德-沃尔团队中，参与那场关于“摄影作为艺术有何用处？”的宏大辩论）——我们想说，他的修正不仅精准，而且必要。它从对一个神话般收藏中指称概念的前期分析出发，抖落了我们词汇表上积满灰尘的地毯：这些图像发表在《Alarma!》（一份墨西哥小报）上，由于缺乏犯罪行为的现场图像，它们借助临时演员——通常是同一犯罪行为的受害者和目击者——来重新演绎犯罪，这些人在图像所指称的犯罪证据前伸出手指指向它们。", studium，这些虚构产物（分类学上奇幻的构图）只要以某种方式被拍摄并呈现，就会带有一种文件的神态。）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此，毫不奇怪，一个其传记中缺失了半截食指的艺术家——更不用说一个摄影师——会对诸如指向这样一个通常如此自发和本能的行为产生如此强烈的意识。（说到底，摄影除了指向-向……之外，还能是什么？）指称性被他体验为一种“暴政”，这是自然的。同样，他与罗兰·巴特的关系因此带有淡淡的怨恨，也就不足为奇了，这使巴特成了他那受损的指示意识的替罪羊或俄狄浦斯式的投射。巴特“绞尽脑汁 [ racked his brains ] （……）为了让摄影依赖于现实”（103），将其构想为并非再现，而是完美的类似物、现实的流溢，其最佳描述无疑是脐带以及控诉的手指。那么，告别时充满控诉的 pathos（悲怆）就颇耐人寻味了。“你，罗兰，拥有所有的手指。而我，却缺了半截食指，”他在临近结尾处写道：“你对我而言是一位宗师、一位引导思想的大师 [ maître-à-penser ]、一位精神之父。话虽如此，为了用自己的头脑思考，必须杀死父亲。”（149-150）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": punctum 的概念。于是发生的情况是，由于不知道拿一张照片怎么办，我们便把它当作语言来对待，然而摄影（在有相反证据证明之前，它并没有“说”过哪怕一个字）却要求被当作文学来对待。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在很大程度上，这种混淆源于对巴特的一种原谅过的犹豫不决：他在全书摇摆不定，有时将 punctum 的概念指定为图像的一种属性，有时又将其视为与图像的关系的一种奇特之处（正如丰库贝塔所想象的那样，这其实是一个主观问题）。反过来，后者似乎认为每张照片所等待的文字对其进行了具体化。它构成了图像的收尾，某种程度上可以说是某种诠释学上的清漆——这暗示着摄影在某种意义上，在经由语言阐明之前并未完成。那么，照片自带图说吗？（照片有 punctum "这种思考摄影的方式暴露出了一系列误解，其中最常见的是倾向于将一种艺术表达方式视为通过孤立图像就能得到充分理解的事物。如果我们称之为“刺点”（punctum）——我们也可以称之为对图像的解读——的事物会根据读者的敏感度和素养而发生（且显著地）变化，从而让人（错误地）以为这是一个“主观”问题；那么它主要还是会根据展示图像的语境而变化，而语境的形式要求往往能将同一张图像变成另一张图像。（例如，如果改变尺度、留白或在序列中的位置等。）孤立的图像只是摄影的多种形态之一，绝非普遍形态，也算不上理解任何图像的最具决定性的因素。这也是摄影师们（他们首先且按定义就是图像收藏者）倾向于将作品成组展示的基本原则之一，而这成组的展示反过来又赋予了某种略显孤立的生活周期以意义。（组织这些作品的思考方式——它不服从任何语法，不服从任何可概括的规则，因此除了艺术家的“语言”或“语调”之外没有任何“语言”（如果这些隐喻有所帮助的话）——这种思考方式对每一幅图像所产生的结果，就是改变其可读性的条件，其塑形能力的极限只取决于组织它们的人，当然，也取决于他们钱包的厚度。）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "另一个同样巨大的误解（大到需要另写一篇文章来讨论）是将“指涉性”（referentiality）、“真实性”和“存在证明”混为一谈，而这种混淆甚至更加频繁。摄影究竟指向什么？它当然指向世界。它当然也指向它自身的形态，而这种形态是否能归结为一根指向一具尸体的手指，实在令人怀疑。它还指向摄影师与相机前事物之间的关系，但首先且最重要的是指向他与相机背后事物之间的关系，在摄影已然非常成熟的阶段，这自然包括了他与摄影史——文学、电影、音乐等历史——之间的关系。两只手根本数不过来，在任何一张照片里究竟有多少根手指指向了多少个方向。然而，对丰古贝尔塔（Fontcuberta）而言，这一切——显而易见——并非新鲜事，但他却退回到了该问题最不有趣的版本中。也许问题在于俄狄浦斯式的焦虑：不仅要杀死父亲，还要杀死对相机的需求，从而杀死对世界的诉求。这一点在一种技术浪漫主义的高峰期表现得尤为明显：这位艺术家预言，通过用人工智能模型取代相机，摄影将转变成“逆向生态描绘”（écfrase reversa），从而让未来的摄影不再是现实的流溢，而是“文本的流溢”（141）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“相机将不再是创造新内容所必需的工具。（……）我们的照片将通过简单的语言指令生成，学习过程将无用武之地，我们将被迫重新审视我们关于真实与记忆、指涉以及‘曾经存在’（ça-a-été）的理论。图像将被带入这个世界，借助的是那些经过训练、力求在每次尝试中都产出完美婴儿的算法助产士。（……）所指将不再被铭刻在图像中，摄影也将不再是现实的流溢，而是转变为文本的流溢。”（140-141）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这段几近狂喜的引文提出了无数棘手的问题，它们远远超出了摄影和艺术世界的范畴，并且在我们已经临近文末时，已无法给出充分的回答。无论如何，值得注意的是，“逆向生态描绘”这一概念如何通过单纯的词项颠覆，背叛了巴特对摄影的理解中所禁锢的那个单义的“刺点”观念——对于这个巴特的指涉教条，无论丰古贝尔塔如何费力挣脱，最终还是无法摆脱。第二个结论将把我们引向进步意欲将“眼/相机文明”（同上）贬入的哀歌般的境地。如果我们失去了与当下的流动、与生活表面的联系，那是多么巨大的遗憾。“曾经存在”（ça-a-été）不过是当我们在个人层面上意识到终结时，当意识到摄影之所以向我们倾诉并非因为它是“指涉性的”，而是因为它向我们展示了我们在死亡那一刻正在失去的一切时，内心感到的一阵紧缩。这是一门半属撒旦的艺术：迷恋世界且乐于堕落，不相信还存在另一个无论如何其光芒都比这个命中注定的星球（连同其所有的优雅与丑陋）更好的世界。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "随之而来的是围绕“太初有道”这一观念的第三个结论。无论人工智能多或少，也许丰古贝尔塔脑海中所想的并不完全叫作“摄影”，甚至也不是“后摄影”，而是插图。对此无可厚非。只是，任何合理的摄影观念都无法经受住对事件顺序的暴力颠覆：这种颠覆剔除了非我——并非作为所指，而是作为将其固定在图像中的冲动之源——一旦从这个星球的表面被抹去，继续留在这里居住还有什么意义？但迟早我们会发现，所有关于价值的问题都将取决于输入（input）的质量。图像的描述性特异性将趋向于取决于逆向生态描绘的敏感度，而如果将这一点留给视频博主和程序员，在我们看来它并不具有前景（无意冒犯）。不，亲爱的若昂（Joan），你所预言的东西需要福楼拜式、纳博科夫式的能力。既然如此，如果我们真能达到那种地步，又何需图像？因为届时将会有文本，既不需要订阅，也不需要算法的曲解。在最好的世界里，未来的摄影就是文学。只不过为此我们已经有了摄影。///",
